This repository is an event-driven AI governance audit pipeline. It turns source events into canonical records, checks them against 16 rules, attaches risk scores, and persists evidence for analysis. A finding records a detected condition; the implemented services do not block a login, stop a deployment, approve a model, or perform remediation.

Scope of this explanation

The implemented producer enum is KEYCLOAK, KUBERNETES, PIPELINE, MODEL_REGISTRY and LLM_GATEWAY. The rule catalog labels are NIST_AI_RMF, ISO_IEC_42001, EU_AI_ACT, NIST_SP_800_53 and GDPR. The earlier eight-producer / ten-framework revamp is not the implementation described here. Framework-to-control values are repository metadata; this document does not independently validate those mappings.

Inferred design intent

Separate services and topic boundaries appear intended to isolate ingestion, rule evaluation and scoring so they can evolve and scale independently. That intent is inferred from the deployment layout; the concrete behavior below is traced to code.

Level 2 · Shared contracts

The data every module exchanges

The contract is shared, but validation strength differs between ingress, Java, Python and SQL.

Purpose
Keep independently deployed components aligned on event and finding shapes.
Inputs
Source-native JSON and rule metadata.
Outputs
A canonical event, zero or more findings, then enriched findings.
Dependencies
JSON Schema at adapter ingress; Java records and Jackson inside Streams; Python dictionaries and SQL constraints downstream.
Interactions
Stable IDs link findings to source events; Kafka keys control partitioning; SQL keys control duplicate rows.
L3Canonical event envelopeExpand
Field groupMeaning and downstream use
schema_version, event_idVersion is "1.0". Adapter UUID5 uses producer + source ID; missing source ID causes UUID4. Source event ID later links a finding to raw_events.
event_time / ingested_atSource time normalized to UTC versus adapter ingestion time. Streams windows use event_time; latency reporting starts at ingested_at.
producer / event_typeProducer selects a rule family. Exact event_type strings select predicates or state updates.
actor / subjectActor requires id/type/roles. Subject requires type/id and can carry namespace, model_name/version and data_classification.
action / outcome / environmentOutcome is SUCCESS, FAILURE or UNKNOWN; environment is dev/test/stage/prod. Most rules do not inspect outcome.
correlation_id / trace_idCorrelation is required; trace_id is optional. Correlation goes into evidence; trace_id is not propagated by FindingFactory.
attributes / labelsAttributes accept arbitrary keys and values at the schema boundary. Labels require string values. Per-event rule attributes are not separately schema-validated.

schemas/governance-event.schema.json:5–64services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:65–84stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/rules/FindingFactory.java:23–35

L3Finding and scored-finding envelopesExpand
Purpose
Represent a rule match and carry it to reporting.
Inputs
RuleDefinition, triggering event, frequency, optional window and extra evidence.
Outputs
Finding fields plus four Python enrichment fields.
Dependencies
FindingFactory, ComplianceFinding record, finding schema, OnlineIsolationScorer.
Interactions
Multiple rules can match one event. The sink writes one row per finding_id.

The factory supplies source_event_time and detected_at separately. Window start/end are present for login bursts. Evidence contains event type, actor ID, subject ID, environment and correlation ID, plus branch-specific fields. It does not copy every source attribute. The scorer adds isolation_forest_risk, risk_delta, recommended_risk and model_status.

Implementation detail

The finding JSON Schema is a documented contract. The inspected rule, scorer and sink paths do not invoke it as a runtime validator. Java deserialization is also not equivalent to the adapter’s JSON Schema validation.

Five adapters, one shared runtime

The adapters receive events. They do not install the external products, subscribe to their logs or configure their audit exporters.

Dependencies

Interactions
Five entry points share one runtime but use distinct producer enums, mappers and default topics.

docker-compose.yml:60–98

L3Shared HTTP runtime and validationExpand
Purpose
Provide a small ingestion boundary and health endpoints.
Inputs
HTTP on 0.0.0.0:PORT, default 8080.
Outputs
JSON responses or text-format event counters.
Dependencies
Shared Adapter instance, standard-library BaseHTTPRequestHandler.
Interactions
POST delegates to publish; readiness asks Kafka for metadata; SIGTERM / SIGINT start server shutdown.
EndpointObserved behavior
POST /eventsContent-Length must be positive and ≤ MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 1,048,576). Returns 202 after publish returns; caught errors return 422.
GET /healthzAlways reports status ok while the HTTP handler is running.
GET /readyzPolls to prime OAuth callbacks, then makes a topic metadata request; 200 or 503. This is not an end-to-end pipeline check.
GET /metricsaccepted/rejected process-local counters, labelled by producer. Counters reset with the process; request errors outside publish do not increment rejected.
Other pathsGET / POST handlers return 404. Standard request logging is suppressed.
Implementation detail

The HTTP runtime uses ThreadingHTTPServer. No FastAPI routing, API authentication, source subscription or source-side audit configuration is implemented in these files. Source systems must push events to these endpoints.

L5Source identity and UTC conversionExpand

UUID5 uses the URL namespace and the producer-specific string. Numeric times above 10,000,000,000 are treated as milliseconds; smaller numeric values are seconds. Digit-only strings reuse numeric conversion. Naive ISO times are treated as UTC; missing time uses now. Unknown outcomes are normalized to UNKNOWN.

services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:26–38services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:65–83

L3Publishing, keys and rejection pathExpand
Purpose
Write canonical events to the adapter’s assigned Kafka topic.
Inputs
Schema-valid GovernanceEvent and topic configuration.
Outputs
Kafka message keyed by actor.id, or model_name:model_version when both are set.
Dependencies
confluent-kafka Producer configured with idempotence, acks=all, zstd and 20 ms linger.
Interactions
Downstream rule and sink consumer groups read independently; POST returns after this method finishes.

The runtime checks the final flush’s remaining-message count, but has no delivery callback that checks each message’s result. Therefore 202 means this code path completed, not that a finding has been generated or stored. A batch is not atomic: earlier items can be produced before a later item fails.

L4Failure side path and dead-letter shapeExpand
Purpose
Retain a diagnostic summary for failures inside the per-item mapping/validation/publish try block.
Inputs
Raw dictionary and exception.
Outputs
producer, source_id, SHA-256 payload_fingerprint, truncated error, received_at.
Dependencies
Kafka dead-letter topic; json.dumps and hashlib.
Interactions
No implemented service consumes this topic. Request JSON/size failures and the final flush timeout are outside this catch block.

The raw object is not stored wholesale in the DLQ record. The error string can still contain values from the rejected event; it is truncated, not redacted. A non-dictionary item can also make the DLQ helper itself fail because it calls raw.get().

Reads id/event_id, time fields, user/auth details, roles and IP. LOGIN_ERROR → LOGIN_FAILURE; LOGIN → LOGIN_SUCCESS; ROLE_MAPPING_CREATE → ROLE_GRANT. Supplied attributes override details. services/producer_adapters/common/mappers.py:48–76

L4Kubernetes audit mapperExpand
Purpose
Translate Kubernetes audit payloads.
Inputs
Native JSON for this source.
Outputs
One mapped event dictionary, not a batch of newly derived events.
Dependencies
Shared _dict, _text, _event_type, _time, _environment, _labels and _subject helpers.
Interactions
Output passes through the shared envelope builder and schema validator.

Create/update/patch of clusterrolebindings maps to CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING; get/list/watch of secrets maps to SECRET_ACCESS; only create of pods maps to POD_CREATE. Pod containers and initContainers are inspected for privileged. Approval/image flags come from governance.example annotations or attributes. cross_namespace defaults false and is not calculated from the service-account namespace. The actor namespace is populated with the target resource namespace. Supplied attributes override computed values.

L5Attribute precedence and operation coverageExpand

The last **supplied merge wins. A missing image-approved annotation produces false in the adapter, whereas a canonical event sent directly to Kafka with image_approved absent uses the Java rule’s default true. Thus the adapter path and direct-fixture path can differ for missing attributes. Audit outcome is recorded but the predicates do not require SUCCESS.

Purpose

Inputs

Dependencies

Interactions

Merges job governance facets, then run governance facets, then raw attributes. Explicit event_type wins, then governance event_type, then OpenLineage eventType. Input/output datasets are not expanded into separate events. A normal COMPLETE event will not itself become DATASET_READ, DRIFT_EVALUATION or BIAS_EVALUATION. runId is the preferred identity: multiple lifecycle events for one run can collide in event_id and raw_events; an event_id fallback does not override a present runId.

A raw prompt key is dropped. Detection, hashing and excerpt redaction are upstream responsibilities; an attribute called redacted_excerpt is accepted as supplied.

L3Topic creation and consumer ownershipExpand
Purpose
Create known topics and give each stage an independent position.
Inputs
Broker address, partition count, replication factor, application/group IDs.
Outputs
Topics and per-group offsets.
Dependencies
Compose rpk loop; Java Admin.createTopics; consumer configurations.
Interactions
Existing-topic errors are tolerated by Java; Compose broadly ignores topic-create errors. No existing topic is reconciled to a new partition/replica setting by this code.

Java defaults to six partitions and replication factor three. Compose creates six partitions with one replica and overrides the Java internal replication factor to one. The rule application ID defaults to governance-rule-engine-v1; Python group IDs default to governance-risk-scorer-v1 and governance-postgres-sink-v1. Changing an ID changes the state/offset namespace. Python consumers use earliest when no valid committed offset exists, not on every restart.

L3Local plaintext and AWS authenticationExpand
Purpose
Select client authentication for the configured broker environment.
Inputs
KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL, bootstrap servers, AWS_REGION and available AWS credentials.

Dependencies

Interactions
EKS service accounts map to IAM roles; adapters get own-topic plus DLQ permissions. Processing services share a broader workload role.

Java’s non-PLAINTEXT path selects AWS_MSK_IAM and supports mechanism/JAAS/callback overrides. Each Python service’s non-PLAINTEXT path explicitly selects OAUTHBEARER and generates tokens with expiry converted from milliseconds to seconds. The Java-specific KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM value in the shared ConfigMap is not read by these Python implementations.

Level 2 → 5 · Detection

The rule engine, branch by branch

Two different kinds of state matter: a time window for failed logins and current model evidence for promotions. Everything else is a direct attribute predicate.

Purpose
Evaluate canonical events and emit auditable rule matches.
Inputs
Five event topics plus the packaged rules.yml catalog.
Outputs
Zero, one or several ComplianceFinding records keyed by finding ID.
Dependencies
Java 21, Kafka Streams 3.9.0, Jackson 2.18.2, MSK IAM library.
Interactions
Stateless checks inspect attributes; login bursts aggregate by identity; promotions join current model evidence.

stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/Application.java:23–37stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:53–68stream-processor/pom.xml:10–35

L3Application startup, catalog and serializationExpand
Purpose
Construct and run the long-lived Streams application.
Inputs
Environment variables and classpath rules.yml.
Outputs
KafkaStreams instance, local state and output records.
Dependencies
Kafka Admin, RuleCatalog, GovernanceTopology and a shutdown latch.
Interactions
Shutdown closes Streams with a 20-second timeout. Uncaught stream-thread exceptions request application shutdown only when state is ERROR; otherwise the handler requests a replacement thread.

The default is two stream threads and state in /tmp/kafka-streams. Commit interval is 1,000 ms. Deserialization uses LogAndContinueExceptionHandler: malformed records can be logged and skipped rather than sent to the adapter DLQ.

L4Catalog loading and typed serializationExpand
Purpose
Provide titles, severities, descriptions and framework lists to executable Java rules.
Inputs
YAML rules array packaged in the application.
Outputs
Immutable ID → RuleDefinition map; missing catalog / wrong count fails startup.
Dependencies
Jackson YAML and RuleDefinition record.
Interactions
Rule logic requests catalog.get(id). YAML changes require a rebuilt/repackaged application; they do not create new executable predicates.

The loader checks 16 unique IDs after map insertion; it does not prove that the IDs are exactly GOV-001 through GOV-016 or validate the regulatory meaning of control mappings. JsonSerde uses a Java-time-aware ObjectMapper and ISO date serialization. Its errors become Kafka SerializationException. EventTimestampExtractor takes event.eventTime when present, then falls back to record time or partition time.

L3Stateless branch · 13 checksExpand
Purpose
Detect conditions that need no history or join.
Inputs
One GovernanceEvent.
Outputs
A list of findings: no match produces an empty list.
Dependencies
RuleCatalog and FindingFactory.
Interactions
Each predicate is a separate if statement, so a gateway event may create three findings. No branch performs an external service lookup.

Thirteen checks live in StatelessRuleEngine. Numeric values accept Number or parseable strings; absent/invalid values become zero. Booleans default false except image_approved and model_approved default true in the Java predicates. There is no general SUCCESS filter, tenant filter or production filter in this stateless branch.

Interactions
source_event_id references the fifth processed qualifying event. The synthetic event hardcodes prod and USER, empty roles, and uses threshold ID as correlation.

These are fixed five-minute buckets, not every possible rolling five-minute interval. A burst split over a bucket boundary can avoid reaching five in either bucket. Grace is an allowance for late event-time records as stream time progresses, not a timer that delays every finding by one minute. No event-ID deduplication is present before counting, and the key contains no realm/tenant dimension. “First” and “fifth” reflect processing order among qualifying records, not a sort of all source timestamps.

Purpose

MODEL_REGISTRY approvals and PIPELINE evaluations with non-null model keys.
Outputs

Interactions
The evaluation filter requires actual Boolean.TRUE, unlike the permissive stateless boolean helper.

There is no expiry/TTL policy in this topology, no revocation or failed-evaluation removal branch, and no required approval/evaluation age. Model keys are not namespaced by environment or tenant.

L5Promotion-time decision and evidence orderingExpand
Purpose
Make a point-in-processing decision on evidence availability.
Inputs
Promotion event and current ModelEvidence from the left join.
Outputs
Up to two findings; promotion event remains the source event for both.
Dependencies
PromotionCheck record and FindingFactory.
Interactions
Later evidence updates do not trigger a replay of the prior promotion, retract findings or mark incidents resolved.

The implementation has no buffering period for late evidence and no explicit event-time “approval occurred before promotion” test. Evidence arriving after the promotion is processed cannot satisfy that already completed check. Conversely, a qualifying row present at lookup time is accepted without a freshness check. The registry mapper’s evaluation alias does not feed the PIPELINE-only evaluation table.

L4Baseline risk arithmeticExpand
FrequencyBandSeverity 4 baseline
≤ 1116
2–3232
4–7348
8–15464
≥ 16580

baseline_risk = clamped severity × frequency band × 4. Stateless checks and promotion checks pass frequency=1. GOV-001 passes frequency=5 at its only emission. Severity labels are low for 1, medium for 2–3, high for 4 and critical for the default branch (catalog severity 5). A critical single-event finding therefore has baseline 20; the label and risk score describe different fields.

Level 2 → 5 · Risk enrichment

From findings to comparative risk

The scorer prioritizes existing findings. It does not discover new rule violations or train on the complete raw-event stream.

Purpose
Add an anomaly-score comparison to findings while retaining the deterministic baseline.
Inputs
governance.findings.raw.v1 JSON records.
Outputs
governance.findings.scored.v1 records with four enrichment fields.
Dependencies
confluent-kafka, NumPy and scikit-learn IsolationForest.
Interactions
Only detected findings enter this model. Benign source events that emitted no finding are not part of its training history.

services/risk-scorer/app.py:41–73services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:27–61

L3Consumer and producer loopExpand
Purpose
Run one scoring pass per consumed finding.
Inputs
Kafka record and scorer process state.
Outputs
Scored Kafka message and committed input offset.
Dependencies
Manual-commit consumer; idempotent producer with acks=all.
Interactions
SIGTERM / SIGINT stop the polling loop; finally closes the consumer and flushes the producer.

The flush return value is not checked and no delivery callback is installed. Output production and input offset commit are separate operations. A crash between them can cause replay; a flush timeout followed by commit can risk loss. JSON or scoring exceptions are not diverted to a DLQ. No HTTP health or metrics server is implemented for this service.

services/risk-scorer/app.py:36–73

L3OnlineIsolationScorer internalsExpand
Purpose
Maintain a bounded recent-finding model in memory.
Inputs
Finding dictionary; min_samples, retrain_every and history_size settings.
Outputs
Enriched copy of the finding; updated in-memory history and optional model.
Dependencies
deque, NumPy arrays and IsolationForest.
Interactions
The current vector is appended before a fit, so a retraining batch includes that current vector. A restart discards model and history and starts warm-up again.

services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:20–40

L4Feature construction · 26 valuesExpand
Feature groupExact constructionInput dependency
Severity / frequency / baselineseverity / 5; frequency_band / 5; baseline_risk / 100All three numeric fields must be present.
Time of daysin(2π × hour / 24), cos(2π × hour / 24)Uses source_event_time.hour; ignores minutes, seconds and weekday.
Rule one-hotOne indicator per GOV-001 through GOV-016Unknown rule IDs yield sixteen zeros.
Producer one-hotOne indicator per the five producer enum stringsUnknown producer yields five zeros.

Numeric timestamps in source_event_time, detected_at and window boundaries are interpreted as epoch seconds for legacy compatibility. ISO timestamp offsets are parsed as supplied; the feature method itself does not convert every string to UTC. It uses no actor, IP, prompt text, model name, dataset contents or per-tenant history.

services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:64–85

L4Fit schedule and scoring policyExpand
Purpose
Decide when to create a fresh forest.
Inputs
History length and since_fit counter.
Outputs
New model with 200 estimators, max_samples=min(256, history length), contamination=auto, random_state=42 and n_jobs=1.
Dependencies
Environment defaults can override sample/retrain/history thresholds.
Interactions
Training runs synchronously inside score(); it is periodic full fitting on the retained deque, not incremental tree updates.

services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:20–40services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:88–93

L5Warm-up, risk transformation and recommended scoreExpand
Purpose
Turn model output into comparable risk fields.
Inputs
Current model decision score and existing baseline_risk.
Outputs
ML risk in 0..100, signed delta, recommended risk and status.
Dependencies
NumPy clip and two-decimal rounding.
Interactions
During warm-up ML and delta are null, recommended risk equals baseline, and status is warming:n/min. Once fitted, status is ready.

The recommended score is the larger of baseline and ML risk. It is not a weighted 70/30 average, and a negative risk_delta does not reduce the recommendation. The score transformation is a repository-defined scale; the code does not calibrate it as a probability of an incident.

services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:42–61

Inferred design intent

A single scorer replica is declared in Kubernetes. Keeping one shared in-process history appears intended to avoid independent models across replicas. This rationale is inferred; scaling to several consumers would give each process its own partition-dependent history.

deploy/k8s/all.yaml:100–127services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:20–25

Level 2 → 4 · Storage

Kafka to PostgreSQL

Two streams converge on the database: canonical events preserve context, and scored findings provide the reportable incidents.

Purpose
Persist canonical event evidence and enriched findings for queries.
Inputs
Six subscribed Kafka topics; PostgreSQL DSN.
Outputs
raw_events and compliance_findings rows.
Dependencies
confluent-kafka, psycopg and the separately initialized SQL schema.
Interactions
The sink consumes raw and finding paths independently. A finding can arrive before its source row; there is no SQL foreign key requiring arrival order.

services/postgres-sink/app.py:13–20services/postgres-sink/app.py:104–137db/001_schema.sql:1–36

L3Connection, dispatch and commitsExpand
Purpose
Drive persistence and reconnect after selected database errors.
Inputs
Kafka messages and database connection availability.
Outputs
Committed rows or a reconnected database handle.
Dependencies
psycopg.OperationalError / InterfaceError handling; manual Kafka commits.
Interactions
Input offset is committed only after the normal SQL commit path completes. Invalid JSON and other uncaught errors can terminate the loop.
Implementation detail

On a caught database error, the code reconnects but neither retries the current record nor seeks its Kafka offset. The next loop polls a new record; a later commit in the same partition can pass the failed one. The code therefore does not establish loss-free database recovery. Stable IDs limit duplicate rows on replay, but do not fix skipped processing.

services/postgres-sink/app.py:42–49services/postgres-sink/app.py:104–137

raw_events and compliance_findings columns; Jsonb serialization.
Interactions
Database commit occurs in the caller, after the selected writer returns.

Level 2 → 4 · User-visible results

Reporting views and Tableau access

A user sees incident and risk data by querying PostgreSQL or connecting an external reporting tool. The optional refresh path provides a local copy of AWS results.

Purpose
Make persisted audit findings consumable by reporting tools.
Inputs
Finding rows, source event ingestion times and stored framework mappings.
Outputs
Queryable views for status counts, risk trends, incident details and latency.
Dependencies
PostgreSQL; external Tableau client; optional refresh script with AWS CLI, kubectl, Docker and Python.
Interactions
The repository supplies data structures and access helpers. No web dashboard application or executable Tableau workbook is implemented in the inspected runtime.

db/001_schema.sql:68–125tableau/refresh_from_aws.sh:26–42

L3View definitions and metric semanticsExpand
ViewInputs → outputsInterpretation
finding_framework_controlsOne finding → one row per framework/control pair.Explodes JSON arrays; one finding can produce many rows.
tableau_framework_statusExpanded rows → per-day, per-framework distinct finding counts, high/critical counts, average/max risk.Counts use DISTINCT finding_id; average_risk is averaged over expanded control rows, so controls weight the mean.
tableau_risk_trendFindings → five-minute buckets by detected_at, producer and rule.Averages baseline, ML and recommended scores; null ML warm-up values are ignored by SQL avg.
tableau_incident_historyFindings → incident rows ordered by detected_at descending.Includes IDs, title, producer, severity label, risk comparison, status and evidence.
tableau_pipeline_latencyFindings JOIN raw_events → five-minute buckets by persisted_at and producer.p50/p95/p99 of finding persisted_at − event ingested_at, in ms. Only joined finding/event pairs contribute.
Implementation detail

Framework counts are counts of mapped findings, not percentages of compliance. No finding-resolution workflow or compliant-control denominator is modeled. Latency is not source-emission-to-user-display time; it excludes events without findings and changes if persisted_at is refreshed on a finding upsert.

db/001_schema.sql:68–125services/postgres-sink/app.py:80–85

Interactions
Incident export replaces the entire evidence object with {"sanitized": true}; it does not selectively redact that object. IDs, titles and other selected fields remain.

The exports are separate source queries, not a single source transaction snapshot. Local publication is grouped into one transaction. The cleanup trap stops port-forwarding, removes the temporary pod/files and unsets the password variable. This documentation build did not run the script or access AWS secrets.

Runtime walkthroughs

What happens, step by step

Startup, a multi-finding request, the stateful rules, negative paths and worker restarts.

These are source-derived walkthroughs. Example payloads and outcomes illustrate the implemented paths; they are not new measurements from a running environment.

L3Flow 1 · Start the local reference stackExpand
  1. Operator trigger: from the repository root, docker compose up --build -d starts the default services. Evaluator and mapper-test services are behind explicit profiles. docker-compose.yml:136–154
  2. Build: the shared adapter Dockerfile copies one selected app.py, common code and event schema. Java builds a shaded JAR with the rule catalog and runs Maven package (which includes its tests). Python worker images start app.py as user 10001. services/producer_adapters/Dockerfile:1–14stream-processor/Dockerfile:1–14services/risk-scorer/Dockerfile:1–10
  3. Infrastructure: Redpanda starts with internal redpanda:9092 and host localhost:19092 listeners. PostgreSQL starts with a named data volume and the schema init script mounted. The PostgreSQL image’s init script applies on first database initialization; this is not a migration runner for an existing volume. docker-compose.yml:10–58
  4. Topics: topic-init waits for broker health and requests eight topics with six partitions / one replica. Adapters and processing workers depend on topic-init completion; sink also waits for PostgreSQL health. docker-compose.yml:1–7docker-compose.yml:30–41docker-compose.yml:100–134
  5. Workers: Java checks/creates topics again, loads 16 catalog entries, builds its topology and starts Streams. Scorer subscribes and initializes an empty model; sink connects and polls. There is no dependency ordering that waits for all workers to be fully caught up before accepting HTTP traffic. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/Application.java:23–35services/risk-scorer/app.py:41–52services/postgres-sink/app.py:104–117
  6. Visible result: adapter ports 8101–8105 accept events and expose health/readiness/metrics. An empty stack does not generate real audit events by itself; sources must send them or the evaluator must inject fixtures. docker-compose.yml:60–98services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:177–206
L3Flow 2 · One gateway request creates three findingsExpand
{
  "request_id": "guide-example-001",
  "event_time": "2026-11-01T09:00:00Z",
  "user_id": "alice",
  "model": {
    "name": "assistant",
    "version": "1"
  },
  "pii_detected": true,
  "pii_handling_allowed": false,
  "model_approved": false,
  "prompt_injection_score": 0.96
}
  1. Trigger: a client posts this illustrative payload to the gateway adapter’s /events. The mapper selects PROMPT_REQUEST, actor alice, model assistant:1 and allowlisted attributes. services/producer_adapters/common/mappers.py:194–223
  2. Normalize and publish: source request ID becomes a producer-scoped UUID5; the event gets ingestion time and schema version. JSON Schema validates it. Kafka key becomes assistant:1. The client receives the event ID in a 202 response after publish returns. services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:65–84services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:135–162services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:196–208
  3. Evaluate: pii_detected with disallowed handling matches GOV-014; model_approved=false matches GOV-015; injection score 0.96 ≥ 0.8 matches GOV-016. Separate if statements emit all three. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/rules/StatelessRuleEngine.java:49–56
  4. Baseline: the catalog severities are 5, 4 and 5; frequency is one for each, so baseline risks are 20, 16 and 20. Each finding gets its own rule-based ID. config/rules.yml:132–161stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/risk/BaselineRiskScorer.java:6–17stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/rules/FindingFactory.java:21–35
  5. Score: during initial warm-up, the recommended scores remain those baselines. After a model is fitted, each recommendation is max(baseline, model risk). No exact future ML number can be promised from this payload alone because history matters. services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:27–61
  6. Persist and view: the sink independently saves the canonical event and the three scored findings. Incident history shows three rows; framework views count them under their configured mappings. The HTTP response itself contains no findings. services/postgres-sink/app.py:113–131db/001_schema.sql:84–113
L3Flow 3 · Five failed logins cross a thresholdExpand
  1. Trigger: five KEYCLOAK LOGIN_FAILURE records for alice at 09:00:00, 09:00:10, 09:00:20, 09:00:30 and 09:00:40 fall in the same 09:00–09:05 bucket. This is an illustrative input sequence.
  2. State transition: each record increments LoginBurst for alice. When count reaches five the aggregate retains the threshold event ID/time. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/model/LoginBurst.java:13–24
  3. Output: count==5 passes the filter. GOV-001 references that threshold event, includes first_event_id and failed_login_count=5, and has severity 4 × band 3 × 4 = 48 baseline risk. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:86–104stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/risk/BaselineRiskScorer.java:6–17
  4. Later events: sixth and subsequent failures in the same window do not update this finding through this branch. A new fixed bucket starts a new aggregate. The downstream scorer and sink handle the emitted finding normally. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:78–87
L3Flow 4 · Model evidence changes a promotion resultExpand
  1. Evidence inputs: a registry APPROVAL_GRANTED for credit:7 updates approval state; a PIPELINE MODEL_EVALUATION_COMPLETED with attributes.passed=true and subject model_name=credit, model_version=7 updates evaluation state. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:111–124
  2. Trigger: a MODEL_REGISTRY MODEL_PROMOTED event in prod with the same model key performs a left join against the current evidence table. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:126–138
  3. Decision: neither row present → GOV-011 and GOV-012; only approval present → GOV-012; only evaluation present → GOV-011; both present → neither finding. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:140–151
  4. User result: missing-evidence findings go to scoring and reporting. The promotion itself is not blocked. Later approval/evaluation events update state for future promotions but do not automatically close earlier findings. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:133–151
L3Flow 5 · A benign event or invalid requestExpand
  1. Benign canonical event: schema-valid data is published and saved by the raw-event sink. If no rule matches, no finding enters the scorer and no incident-history row is created. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:55–66stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/rules/StatelessRuleEngine.java:15–24services/postgres-sink/app.py:126–129
  2. Invalid mapped item: a per-item exception increments rejected and attempts a diagnostic DLQ record, then returns an HTTP error through the handler. A batch can already have published earlier items. services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:135–159
  3. Invalid request body: bad size or invalid JSON is caught in do_POST and returned as 422, before the per-item DLQ path. No service here automatically retries or replays the DLQ. services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:196–208services/postgres-sink/app.py:13–20
L3Flow 6 · Stop and restart a workerExpand
  1. Streams: the shutdown hook closes KafkaStreams. A replacement uses the configured application ID and named stores; Kafka Streams provides changelog-backed restoration for the materialized stores. No application-specific restore loop is implemented. stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/Application.java:28–35stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:79–83stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:111–130
  2. Scorer: consumer offsets can resume, but its deque/model are process-local and are rebuilt from subsequent consumed findings. Historical model state is not serialized. services/risk-scorer/app.py:44–52services/risk-scorer/scorer.py:20–25
  3. Sink: PostgreSQL rows persist separately. Replayed event IDs are ignored and finding scores are updated. This does not guarantee replay of a record skipped after the reconnect path described earlier. services/postgres-sink/app.py:52–96services/postgres-sink/app.py:125–134
  4. Deployment storage: Kubernetes Streams state is an emptyDir; local Compose declares a named volume only for PostgreSQL, not Redpanda or Streams. A broker container restart and a broker container replacement are different durability scenarios. deploy/k8s/all.yaml:49–67docker-compose.yml:10–28docker-compose.yml:156–157

Where behavior is configured

Code defaults are shown explicitly. This section also covers settings that cannot be changed through environment variables.

ScriptWhat it actually doesSource
pause_services.shStops local PostgreSQL; deletes all HPAs and scales all Deployments in the namespace to zero; sets node desired/min to zero; requests RDS stop only if status is available. It leaves MSK/EKS control-plane resources provisioned.ops/pause_services.sh:13–37
resume_services.shStarts local PostgreSQL; starts RDS if stopped; sets nodes to 3; waits for node group, RDS and nodes; sets engine=3, scorer=1, sink=2, adapters=2; recreates CPU HPAs for engine/adapters and waits for rollouts.ops/resume_services.sh:13–67

The scripts restore fixed replica counts, not a captured previous state. The resume script’s kubectl autoscale command does not reproduce the manifest’s explicit 300-second scale-down behavior. Namespace-wide pause commands also affect other Deployments/HPAs if placed in the same namespace.

Level 2 → 3 · Verification tools

What the repository tests and measures

The evaluation harness is a support module. Its generated fixtures and stored result notes should be distinguished from current deployment status.

Purpose
Exercise implemented checks and summarize persisted detection results.
Inputs
CLI subcommand, repeat/delay/wait arguments, broker and database settings.
Outputs
Synthetic events, evaluation tables, JSON reports and optional induced restart experiments.
Dependencies
confluent-kafka, jsonschema, NumPy, psycopg; urllib for adapter smoke tests.
Interactions
Direct injection bypasses native adapters. Adapter smoke tests cover one native example per adapter. Reporting is based on stored finding pairs, not a continuous external monitoring system.

evaluation/evaluator.py:97–135evaluation/evaluator.py:142–211evaluation/evaluator.py:214–275

L3Fixture generator and direct injectionExpand
Purpose
Build a repeatable labelled workload around the 16 rules.
Inputs
Repeat index, base timestamp and unique run tag.
Outputs
24 events and 16 expected (event_id, rule_id) matches per repeat; defaults yield 72 events / 48 matches.
Dependencies
envelope(), scenarios(), event JSON Schema and evaluation tables.
Interactions
Five failed-login records share a unique actor. One promotion yields two expected findings. Five benign controls test negative paths.

The injector writes ground truth before publishing. It keys events by actor or model, but does not set the Kafka message timestamp; Streams still uses the envelope event_time through its extractor. Flush(30) is called without checking the result. Its Kafka producer config has no implemented IAM authentication branch, unlike the runtime adapters. The base timestamp is not aligned to a five-minute boundary, so the five login events can straddle a window boundary near that edge.

evaluation/evaluator.py:27–94evaluation/evaluator.py:97–135stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:76–78

L3Report calculation and metric boundariesExpand
Purpose
Compute evaluation metrics for the most recently started run.
Inputs
evaluation_runs, expected triples, event membership and persisted findings.
Outputs
Precision, recall, TP/FP/FN, latency percentiles, throughput and run results JSON.
Dependencies
SQL queries, Python set operations and NumPy percentile.
Interactions
Actual detections are distinct (source_event_id, rule_id) pairs scoped to run event IDs. Duplicate findings are collapsed for this comparison.
MetricImplementation and limit
Precision / recallTP = expected ∩ actual; FP = actual − expected; FN = expected − actual. No true-negative count or accuracy metric is computed.
Wait conditionStops when observed count reaches expected_count or timeout expires; it does not wait for a proof of pipeline quiescence.
LatencyFinding persisted_at minus canonical ingested_at, clamped to ≥0 in evaluator; only joined finding/event rows are measured.
ThroughputRaw row count divided by max persisted_at − min persisted_at, floored at 0.001 seconds. This is a persistence-span estimate, not an externally timed sustained load benchmark.
Run selectionAlways latest started run; no --run-id option. Concurrent runs can change which one is reported.

evaluation/evaluator.py:142–211

L3HTTP smoke and restart experimentsExpand
Purpose
Exercise the native ingestion path and local interruption scenarios.
Inputs
Five built-in HTTP samples; processor|broker argument for local_resilience.sh.
Outputs
Smoke JSON with missing pairs; failure exit if expected pairs are absent; restart-time output and evaluator report.
Dependencies
Running adapters, workers, Kafka, PostgreSQL and Docker Compose.
Interactions
Smoke checks for the expected subset, not absence of every extra finding. The local restart script waits for at least ten new raw rows during injection, then replaces the processor container or restarts Redpanda.

Implementation detail

evaluation/RESULTS.md records local measurements dated 2026-10-04, including 72-event / 48-finding runs and a 5/5 adapter smoke result. Those are historical repository notes, not tests rerun while creating this page. The current explanation was checked against source and the HTML was verified separately; no AWS failure experiment or live pipeline benchmark was run.

evaluation/RESULTS.md:1–14

The present test files do not establish positive approval/evaluation joins, every missing-attribute case, source-ID collision safety, duplicate-aware windows or recovery from all sink/scorer failure positions. The documented three-broker AWS exercise remains a procedure, not evidence of an executed run.

evaluation/RESILIENCE.md:1–29

Reading the implementation accurately

Behavior boundaries that affect interpretation

These observations explain what the current code can support. They are not a restart of the paused revamp plan.

BoundaryObserved implementationEvidence
Source integrationsHTTP receivers and mapping functions exist. Source-side exporters/subscriptions must provide events and policy signals.services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:165–219services/producer_adapters/common/mappers.py:48–76
Governance analysisRules compare supplied drift, bias, PII, approval and signature signals; they do not calculate all those signals or verify a signature cryptographically.stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/rules/StatelessRuleEngine.java:38–52
Ingestion identityOpenLineage runId takes precedence over event_id; repeated lifecycle events may share an ID. Streams does not deduplicate before the burst aggregate.services/producer_adapters/common/mappers.py:146services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:65–71stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:74–87
Decision statePromotion decisions use currently stored qualifying evidence. No revocation, expiration, delayed recheck or incident resolution path is implemented.stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/streams/GovernanceTopology.java:111–151
DeliveryStreams enables exactly-once v2, but scorer publishing/offset commit and SQL/offset commits are separate. Scorer does not check flush count; sink reconnect does not replay the failed record.stream-processor/src/main/java/io/governance/Application.java:85services/risk-scorer/app.py:64–70services/postgres-sink/app.py:125–134
Schema enforcementEvent shape validated at adapters/evaluator. Attribute-specific business requirements are not enforced by the generic JSON Schema. Finding schema is not called by scorer/sink.schemas/governance-event.schema.json:29–33services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:139–140services/risk-scorer/app.py:62–70services/postgres-sink/app.py:124–131
Privacy boundaryGateway mapping excludes raw prompt keys, but accepts redacted_excerpt and policy signals as provided. DLQ error text is truncated without redaction.services/producer_adapters/common/mappers.py:197–203services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:122–133
User experienceHTTP acceptance responses, queryable SQL views and CLI JSON reports exist. A dedicated web UI, alert notification dispatcher, case-management lifecycle and automated remediation are not wired into these runtime paths.services/producer_adapters/common/runtime.py:196–208db/001_schema.sql:84–125evaluation/evaluator.py:194–211
Operational stateTerraform/manifests express intended infrastructure; placeholders and separately provisioned secrets/schema remain part of deployment. This page does not inspect live AWS resources.deploy/k8s/all.yaml:12–24deploy/k8s/all.yaml:149–154

SHA-256: f92f1c2921c12286ef58c4612d2a5d8038beda93fc2a6970227ee7b12cb1f533

1CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS raw_events (
2  event_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
3  schema_version TEXT NOT NULL,
4  producer TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (producer IN ('KEYCLOAK','KUBERNETES','PIPELINE','MODEL_REGISTRY','LLM_GATEWAY')),
5  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
6  event_time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
7  ingested_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
8  environment TEXT NOT NULL,
9  correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL,
10  payload JSONB NOT NULL,
11  persisted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
12);
13 
14CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS compliance_findings (
15  finding_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
16  rule_id TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (rule_id ~ '^GOV-[0-9]{3}$'),
17  title TEXT NOT NULL,
18  producer TEXT NOT NULL,
19  source_event_id UUID NOT NULL,
20  source_event_time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
21  detected_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
22  window_start TIMESTAMPTZ,
23  window_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
24  severity SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (severity BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
25  severity_label TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity_label IN ('low','medium','high','critical')),
26  frequency INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (frequency > 0),
27  frequency_band SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (frequency_band BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
28  baseline_risk NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (baseline_risk BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
29  isolation_forest_risk NUMERIC(5,2) CHECK (isolation_forest_risk BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
30  risk_delta NUMERIC(6,2),
31  recommended_risk NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (recommended_risk BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
32  model_status TEXT,
33  frameworks JSONB NOT NULL,
34  evidence JSONB NOT NULL,
35  persisted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
36);
37 
38CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evaluation_ground_truth (
39  run_id UUID NOT NULL,
40  event_id UUID NOT NULL,
41  expected_rule_id TEXT NOT NULL,
42  injected_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
43  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, event_id, expected_rule_id)
44);
45 
46CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evaluation_events (
47  run_id UUID NOT NULL,
48  event_id UUID NOT NULL,
49  injected_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
50  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, event_id)
51);
52 
53CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evaluation_runs (
54  run_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
55  started_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
56  expected_findings INTEGER NOT NULL,
57  injected_events INTEGER NOT NULL,
58  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
59  results JSONB
60);
61 
62CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_raw_event_time ON raw_events (event_time DESC);
63CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_raw_producer ON raw_events (producer, event_time DESC);
64CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_findings_detected ON compliance_findings (detected_at DESC);
65CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_findings_rule ON compliance_findings (rule_id, detected_at DESC);
66CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_findings_frameworks ON compliance_findings USING GIN (frameworks);
67 
68CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW finding_framework_controls AS
69SELECT
70  f.finding_id,
71  f.rule_id,
72  f.title,
73  f.detected_at,
74  f.producer,
75  f.severity,
76  f.severity_label,
77  f.recommended_risk,
78  framework.key AS framework,
79  control.value #>> '{}' AS control
80FROM compliance_findings f
81CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(f.frameworks) AS framework(key, controls)
82CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(framework.controls) AS control(value);
83 
84CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tableau_framework_status AS
85SELECT
86  date_trunc('day', detected_at) AS day,
87  framework,
88  count(DISTINCT finding_id) AS finding_count,
89  count(DISTINCT finding_id) FILTER (WHERE severity >= 4) AS high_or_critical_count,
90  round(avg(recommended_risk), 2) AS average_risk,
91  max(recommended_risk) AS maximum_risk
92FROM finding_framework_controls
93GROUP BY 1, 2;
94 
95CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tableau_risk_trend AS
96SELECT
97  date_bin('5 minutes', detected_at, TIMESTAMPTZ '2020-01-01') AS time_bucket,
98  producer,
99  rule_id,
100  round(avg(baseline_risk), 2) AS baseline_risk,
101  round(avg(isolation_forest_risk), 2) AS isolation_forest_risk,
102  round(avg(recommended_risk), 2) AS recommended_risk,
103  count(*) AS finding_count
104FROM compliance_findings
105GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;
106 
107CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tableau_incident_history AS
108SELECT
109  finding_id, detected_at, rule_id, title, producer, severity_label,
110  baseline_risk, isolation_forest_risk, risk_delta, recommended_risk,
111  model_status, source_event_id, evidence
112FROM compliance_findings
113ORDER BY detected_at DESC;
114 
115CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tableau_pipeline_latency AS
116SELECT
117  date_bin('5 minutes', f.persisted_at, TIMESTAMPTZ '2020-01-01') AS time_bucket,
118  f.producer,
119  percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (f.persisted_at - r.ingested_at)) * 1000) AS p50_ms,
120  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (f.persisted_at - r.ingested_at)) * 1000) AS p95_ms,
121  percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (f.persisted_at - r.ingested_at)) * 1000) AS p99_ms,
122  count(*) AS samples
123FROM compliance_findings f
124JOIN raw_events r ON r.event_id = f.source_event_id
125GROUP BY 1, 2;

SHA-256: fa8d22d46eb18ad9e24bbc872e201fc7dfad24f76d8389fd415f84d783a69af8

1# Resilience evaluation
2 
3Before the AWS test, run `evaluation/local_resilience.sh processor` and `evaluation/local_resilience.sh broker`. Each smoke test publishes the labelled workload at 10 events per second while introducing the fault, then reruns the same precision, recall, latency, throughput, and database reconciliation report. The local broker restart checks client retry and durable consumption behavior; the three-broker MSK procedure below measures broker failover.
4 
5Run the labelled injection first and record the latest `evaluation_runs` row. Capture topic end offsets and the consumer-group lag for `governance-rule-engine-v1`, `governance-risk-scorer-v1`, and `governance-postgres-sink-v1`.
6 
7## Processor pod failure
8 
91. Continuously inject at a fixed rate for at least five minutes.
102. Delete one rule-engine pod: `kubectl delete pod -n governance -l app=governance-rule-engine --field-selector=status.phase=Running --wait=false`.
113. Record rebalance duration from Kafka consumer-group metrics and the time until the replacement pod is ready.
124. After lag returns to zero, verify that every injected event exists in `raw_events`, finding IDs remain unique, and precision/recall are unchanged.
13 
14The expected result is a short lag spike, consumer-group reassignment to the remaining replicas, no duplicate database rows, and no missing labelled findings.
15 
16## MSK broker failure
17 
18Use a non-production cluster and an approved test window. Record partition leaders and offsets, then reboot exactly one broker with the MSK `RebootBroker` API. Keep the event generator running throughout the reboot. Track under-replicated partitions, producer errors, consumer lag, recovery time, and database counts. Replication factor 3 and `acks=all` should preserve acknowledged records.
19 
20The broker test passes when all partitions return in-sync, lag drains to zero, every acknowledged injected event is present, and the evaluation result has no new false negatives. Do not terminate two brokers at once in the three-broker test cluster.
21 
22## Evidence to retain
23 
24- UTC start/end times and git commit.
25- Input rate and total acknowledged events.
26- Consumer lag and rebalance/recovery duration.
27- Before/after partition offsets and database row counts.
28- Precision, recall, p50/p95/p99 latency, and throughput report.
29- CloudWatch screenshots or exported metrics for MSK, EKS, and RDS.
evaluation/RESULTS.md14 lines · SHA-256 a2e34f1b713d

SHA-256: a2e34f1b713d65c466b03ee50e8d25af318c6c170f5b3c2fd114c61c162230bf

1# Local evaluation results
2 
3Measured on 2026-10-04 with the Docker Compose reference stack. Each run covered all 16 rules and compared the detected `(event_id, rule_id)` pairs with labelled ground truth.
4 
5| Scenario | Events | Expected / observed | Precision | Recall | p50 / p95 / p99 latency | Throughput | Fault recovery |
6|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
7| Baseline | 72 | 48 / 48 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 2,275 / 3,113 / 3,139 ms | 130.90 events/s | n/a |
8| Processor replacement during injection | 72 | 48 / 48 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 47,298 / 48,338 / 48,352 ms | 11.50 events/s | Container replaced in 3 s; backlog drained with no loss |
9| Broker restart during injection | 72 | 48 / 48 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 7,538 / 7,919 / 7,931 ms | 11.48 events/s | Broker restarted in 1 s; producer retried with no loss |
10| Independent-service regression baseline | 72 | 48 / 48 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1,620 / 2,710 / 2,724 ms | 667.12 events/s | Five standalone producer adapters running |
11 
12The recovery runs intentionally publish at 10 events per second so the fault occurs during the workload. Latency includes injection, outage, consumer recovery, risk scoring, and PostgreSQL persistence. The local single-broker test verifies retry and durable recovery behavior. The three-broker MSK failover procedure in `RESILIENCE.md` must be run in the target AWS account to measure partition-leader failover and replica recovery.
13 
14The independent-adapter smoke test posted one native event to each of the five separate HTTP services. All five were normalized, schema validated, written to their assigned topics, detected by the rule engine, scored, and persisted. It observed 5/5 expected findings. A raw prompt marker sent to the LLM adapter was absent from both the canonical event attributes and the PostgreSQL JSON payload.

1from __future__ import annotations
2 
3import argparse
4from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
5import json
6import os
7import time
8from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
9import uuid
10 
11from confluent_kafka import Producer
12from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker
13import numpy as np
14import psycopg
15from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
16 
17 
18TOPICS = {
19    "KEYCLOAK": "governance.keycloak.v1",
20    "KUBERNETES": "governance.kubernetes.v1",
21    "PIPELINE": "governance.pipeline.v1",
22    "MODEL_REGISTRY": "governance.model-registry.v1",
23    "LLM_GATEWAY": "governance.llm-gateway.v1",
24}
25 
26 
27def envelope(producer, event_type, attributes, at, *, actor="evaluation-user", subject=None, environment="prod"):
28    event_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
29    model_name, model_version = (subject or {}).get("model_name"), (subject or {}).get("model_version")
30    return {
31        "schema_version": "1.0",
32        "event_id": event_id,
33        "event_time": at.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
34        "ingested_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
35        "producer": producer,
36        "event_type": event_type,
37        "actor": {"id": actor, "type": "USER", "roles": [], "ip": "192.0.2.10", "namespace": "team-a"},
38        "subject": {
39            "type": (subject or {}).get("type", "RESOURCE"),
40            "id": (subject or {}).get("id", f"fixture-{event_id}"),
41            "namespace": (subject or {}).get("namespace"),
42            "model_name": model_name,
43            "model_version": model_version,
44            "data_classification": (subject or {}).get("data_classification"),
45        },
46        "action": event_type.lower(),
47        "outcome": "FAILURE" if event_type == "LOGIN_FAILURE" else "SUCCESS",
48        "environment": environment,
49        "correlation_id": f"evaluation-{event_id}",
50        "trace_id": None,
51        "attributes": attributes,
52        "labels": {"synthetic": "true"},
53    }
54 
55 
56def scenarios(repeat, base, run_tag="fixture"):
57    events = []
58    expected = []
59 
60    def add(event, *rules):
61        events.append(event)
62        expected.extend((event["event_id"], rule) for rule in rules)
63 
64    user = f"burst-user-{run_tag}-{repeat}"
65    for index in range(5):
66        login = envelope("KEYCLOAK", "LOGIN_FAILURE", {}, base + timedelta(seconds=index), actor=user)
67        if index == 4:
68            add(login, "GOV-001")
69        else:
70            add(login)
71    add(envelope("KEYCLOAK", "ROLE_GRANT", {"privileged_role": True, "change_approved": False}, base + timedelta(seconds=6)), "GOV-002")
72    add(envelope("KEYCLOAK", "LOGIN_SUCCESS", {"privileged_identity": True, "mfa_used": False}, base + timedelta(seconds=7)), "GOV-003")
73    add(envelope("KUBERNETES", "CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING", {"cluster_role": "cluster-admin", "change_approved": False}, base + timedelta(seconds=8)), "GOV-004")
74    add(envelope("KUBERNETES", "SECRET_ACCESS", {"cross_namespace": True}, base + timedelta(seconds=9)), "GOV-005")
75    add(envelope("KUBERNETES", "POD_CREATE", {"privileged": True, "image_approved": True}, base + timedelta(seconds=10)), "GOV-006")
76    add(envelope("PIPELINE", "DATASET_READ", {"dataset_owner": ""}, base + timedelta(seconds=11)), "GOV-007")
77    add(envelope("PIPELINE", "SCHEMA_CHANGE", {"version_bumped": False}, base + timedelta(seconds=12)), "GOV-008")
78    add(envelope("PIPELINE", "DRIFT_EVALUATION", {"metric_value": 0.35, "threshold": 0.20, "remediation_status": "NOT_STARTED"}, base + timedelta(seconds=13)), "GOV-009")
79    add(envelope("PIPELINE", "BIAS_EVALUATION", {"metric_value": 0.19, "threshold": 0.10, "approved_exception": False}, base + timedelta(seconds=14)), "GOV-010")
80    model_version = f"{run_tag}-{repeat}"
81    model = {"type": "MODEL", "id": f"credit-risk:{model_version}", "model_name": "credit-risk", "model_version": model_version}
82    add(envelope("MODEL_REGISTRY", "MODEL_PROMOTED", {}, base + timedelta(seconds=15), subject=model), "GOV-011", "GOV-012")
83    add(envelope("MODEL_REGISTRY", "ARTIFACT_REGISTERED", {"signature_verified": False, "sha256": ""}, base + timedelta(seconds=16), subject=model), "GOV-013")
84    add(envelope("LLM_GATEWAY", "PROMPT_REQUEST", {"pii_detected": True, "pii_handling_allowed": False, "model_approved": True, "prompt_injection_score": 0.1}, base + timedelta(seconds=17)), "GOV-014")
85    add(envelope("LLM_GATEWAY", "PROMPT_REQUEST", {"pii_detected": False, "model_approved": False, "prompt_injection_score": 0.1}, base + timedelta(seconds=18)), "GOV-015")
86    add(envelope("LLM_GATEWAY", "PROMPT_REQUEST", {"pii_detected": False, "model_approved": True, "prompt_injection_score": 0.96}, base + timedelta(seconds=19)), "GOV-016")
87 
88    # Five benign controls exercise negative cases and contribute to precision measurement.
89    add(envelope("KEYCLOAK", "LOGIN_SUCCESS", {"privileged_identity": True, "mfa_used": True}, base + timedelta(seconds=20)))
90    add(envelope("KUBERNETES", "POD_CREATE", {"privileged": False, "image_approved": True}, base + timedelta(seconds=21)))
91    add(envelope("PIPELINE", "SCHEMA_CHANGE", {"version_bumped": True}, base + timedelta(seconds=22)))
92    add(envelope("MODEL_REGISTRY", "ARTIFACT_REGISTERED", {"signature_verified": True, "sha256": "abc123"}, base + timedelta(seconds=23), subject=model))
93    add(envelope("LLM_GATEWAY", "PROMPT_REQUEST", {"pii_detected": False, "model_approved": True, "prompt_injection_score": 0.02}, base + timedelta(seconds=24)))
94    return events, expected
95 
96 
97def inject(args):
98    with open("governance-event.schema.json") as schema_file:
99        validator = Draft202012Validator(json.load(schema_file), format_checker=FormatChecker())
100    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": os.getenv("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "localhost:19092"), "enable.idempotence": True, "acks": "all"})
101    run_id = uuid.uuid4()
102    all_events, all_expected = [], []
103    base = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0) - timedelta(seconds=5)
104    for repeat in range(args.repeats):
105        run_events, run_expected = scenarios(repeat + 1, base, str(run_id)[:8])
106        all_events.extend(run_events)
107        all_expected.extend(run_expected)
108    for event in all_events:
109        validator.validate(event)
110 
111    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["POSTGRES_DSN"]) as connection:
112        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
113            cursor.execute(
114                "INSERT INTO evaluation_runs (run_id, expected_findings, injected_events) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
115                (run_id, len(all_expected), len(all_events)),
116            )
117            cursor.executemany(
118                "INSERT INTO evaluation_events (run_id, event_id) VALUES (%s, %s)",
119                [(run_id, event["event_id"]) for event in all_events],
120            )
121            cursor.executemany(
122                "INSERT INTO evaluation_ground_truth (run_id, event_id, expected_rule_id) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
123                [(run_id, event_id, rule) for event_id, rule in all_expected],
124            )
125 
126    for event in all_events:
127        key = event["actor"]["id"]
128        if event["subject"].get("model_name") and event["subject"].get("model_version"):
129            key = f'{event["subject"]["model_name"]}:{event["subject"]["model_version"]}'
130        producer.produce(TOPICS[event["producer"]], key=key.encode(), value=json.dumps(event).encode())
131        producer.poll(0)
132        if args.delay_ms > 0:
133            time.sleep(args.delay_ms / 1000)
134    producer.flush(30)
135    print(json.dumps({"run_id": str(run_id), "events": len(all_events), "expected_findings": len(all_expected)}, indent=2))
136 
137 
138def percentile(values, q):
139    return round(float(np.percentile(np.asarray(values), q)), 2) if values else None
140 
141 
142def report(args):
143    dsn = os.environ["POSTGRES_DSN"]
144    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as connection:
145        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
146            cursor.execute("SELECT run_id, expected_findings FROM evaluation_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1")
147            latest = cursor.fetchone()
148            if latest is None:
149                raise SystemExit("No evaluation run found. Run 'inject' first.")
150            run_id, expected_count = latest
151        deadline = time.time() + args.wait
152        while True:
153            with connection.cursor() as cursor:
154                cursor.execute(
155                    """SELECT count(*) FROM compliance_findings f
156                       JOIN evaluation_events e ON e.run_id=%s AND e.event_id=f.source_event_id""",
157                    (run_id,),
158                )
159                observed = cursor.fetchone()[0]
160            if observed >= expected_count or time.time() >= deadline:
161                break
162            time.sleep(2)
163 
164        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
165            cursor.execute("SELECT event_id::text, expected_rule_id FROM evaluation_ground_truth WHERE run_id=%s", (run_id,))
166            expected = set(cursor.fetchall())
167            cursor.execute(
168                """SELECT DISTINCT f.source_event_id::text, f.rule_id
169                   FROM compliance_findings f
170                   WHERE f.source_event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM evaluation_events WHERE run_id=%s)""",
171                (run_id,),
172            )
173            actual = set(cursor.fetchall())
174            cursor.execute(
175                """SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (f.persisted_at-r.ingested_at))*1000
176                   FROM compliance_findings f JOIN raw_events r ON r.event_id=f.source_event_id
177                   WHERE r.event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM evaluation_events WHERE run_id=%s)""",
178                (run_id,),
179            )
180            latencies = [max(0.0, float(row[0])) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
181            cursor.execute(
182                """SELECT count(*), EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (max(persisted_at)-min(persisted_at)))
183                   FROM raw_events WHERE event_id IN
184                   (SELECT event_id FROM evaluation_events WHERE run_id=%s)""",
185                (run_id,),
186            )
187            event_count, duration = cursor.fetchone()
188 
189            true_positive = len(expected & actual)
190            false_positive = len(actual - expected)
191            false_negative = len(expected - actual)
192            precision = true_positive / (true_positive + false_positive) if true_positive + false_positive else 0
193            recall = true_positive / (true_positive + false_negative) if true_positive + false_negative else 0
194            result = {
195                "run_id": str(run_id),
196                "true_positive": true_positive,
197                "false_positive": false_positive,
198                "false_negative": false_negative,
199                "precision": round(precision, 4),
200                "recall": round(recall, 4),
201                "latency_ms": {"p50": percentile(latencies, 50), "p95": percentile(latencies, 95), "p99": percentile(latencies, 99)},
202                "throughput_events_per_second": round(event_count / max(float(duration or 0), 0.001), 2),
203                "observed_findings": len(actual),
204                "expected_findings": len(expected),
205            }
206            cursor.execute(
207                "UPDATE evaluation_runs SET completed_at=now(), results=%s WHERE run_id=%s",
208                (Jsonb(result), run_id),
209            )
210        connection.commit()
211    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
212 
213 
214def adapter_smoke(args):
215    marker = str(uuid.uuid4())
216    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
217    samples = [
218        (
219            os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_ADAPTER_URL", "http://keycloak-adapter:8080/events"),
220            {"id": f"kc-{marker}", "time": now, "type": "ROLE_MAPPING_CREATE", "userId": "smoke-user", "attributes": {"privileged_role": True, "change_approved": False}},
221            "GOV-002",
222        ),
223        (
224            os.getenv("KUBERNETES_ADAPTER_URL", "http://kubernetes-audit-adapter:8080/events"),
225            {"auditID": f"ka-{marker}", "requestReceivedTimestamp": now, "verb": "create", "user": {"username": "smoke-admin"}, "objectRef": {"resource": "clusterrolebindings", "name": "smoke-binding"}, "requestObject": {"roleRef": {"name": "cluster-admin"}}},
226            "GOV-004",
227        ),
228        (
229            os.getenv("PIPELINE_ADAPTER_URL", "http://airflow-openlineage-adapter:8080/events"),
230            {"eventTime": now, "eventType": "COMPLETE", "run": {"runId": f"run-{marker}", "facets": {"governance": {"event_type": "DRIFT_EVALUATION", "metric_value": 0.4, "threshold": 0.2, "remediation_status": "NOT_STARTED"}}}, "job": {"namespace": "airflow", "name": "smoke-drift"}},
231            "GOV-009",
232        ),
233        (
234            os.getenv("MODEL_REGISTRY_ADAPTER_URL", "http://model-registry-adapter:8080/events"),
235            {"id": f"mr-{marker}", "event_time": now, "action": "artifact_created", "model": {"name": "smoke-model", "version": marker[:8]}, "attributes": {"signature_verified": False, "sha256": ""}},
236            "GOV-013",
237        ),
238        (
239            os.getenv("LLM_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_URL", "http://llm-gateway-adapter:8080/events"),
240            {"request_id": f"llm-{marker}", "event_time": now, "user_id": "smoke-user", "prompt": "must not be persisted", "pii_detected": True, "pii_handling_allowed": False, "model_approved": True, "prompt_injection_score": 0.1, "model": {"name": "smoke-llm", "version": "1"}},
241            "GOV-014",
242        ),
243    ]
244    expected = set()
245    for url, payload, rule_id in samples:
246        request = Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
247        with urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
248            result = json.load(response)
249        if result.get("accepted") != 1:
250            raise RuntimeError(f"Adapter at {url} did not accept exactly one event: {result}")
251        expected.add((result["event_ids"][0], rule_id))
252 
253    deadline = time.time() + args.wait
254    actual = set()
255    event_ids = [event_id for event_id, _ in expected]
256    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["POSTGRES_DSN"]) as connection:
257        while time.time() < deadline:
258            with connection.cursor() as cursor:
259                cursor.execute(
260                    "SELECT source_event_id::text, rule_id FROM compliance_findings WHERE source_event_id = ANY(%s::uuid[])",
261                    (event_ids,),
262                )
263                actual = set(cursor.fetchall())
264            if expected <= actual:
265                break
266            time.sleep(1)
267    result = {
268        "adapters_tested": 5,
269        "expected_findings": len(expected),
270        "observed_findings": len(expected & actual),
271        "missing": sorted(expected - actual),
272    }
273    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
274    if expected - actual:
275        raise SystemExit(1)
276 
277 
278def main():
279    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
280    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
281    inject_parser = subparsers.add_parser("inject")
282    inject_parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3)
283    inject_parser.add_argument("--delay-ms", type=float, default=0, help="Delay between events for failure testing")
284    inject_parser.set_defaults(function=inject)
285    report_parser = subparsers.add_parser("report")
286    report_parser.add_argument("--wait", type=int, default=90)
287    report_parser.set_defaults(function=report)
288    adapter_parser = subparsers.add_parser("adapter-smoke")
289    adapter_parser.add_argument("--wait", type=int, default=90)
290    adapter_parser.set_defaults(function=adapter_smoke)
291    args = parser.parse_args()
292    args.function(args)
293 
294 
295if __name__ == "__main__":
296    main()

1#!/usr/bin/env bash
2set -euo pipefail
3 
4case_name="${1:-}"
5if [[ "$case_name" != "processor" && "$case_name" != "broker" ]]; then
6  echo "Usage: evaluation/local_resilience.sh processor|broker" >&2
7  exit 2
8fi
9 
10project_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
11cd "$project_dir"
12 
13raw_event_count() {
14  docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U governance -d governance -Atqc \
15    "SELECT count(*) FROM raw_events"
16}
17 
18before="$(raw_event_count)"
19output_file="$(mktemp)"
20trap 'rm -f "$output_file"' EXIT
21 
22docker compose --profile evaluation run --rm evaluator inject --delay-ms 100 >"$output_file" &
23inject_pid=$!
24 
25deadline=$((SECONDS + 60))
26while (( $(raw_event_count) < before + 10 )); do
27  if ! kill -0 "$inject_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
28    wait "$inject_pid"
29    echo "Injection ended before the failure could be introduced." >&2
30    exit 1
31  fi
32  if (( SECONDS >= deadline )); then
33    echo "Timed out waiting for the workload to start." >&2
34    exit 1
35  fi
36  sleep 0.25
37done
38 
39fault_started="$(date +%s)"
40if [[ "$case_name" == "processor" ]]; then
41  docker compose stop stream-processor
42  docker compose rm -f stream-processor
43  docker compose up -d stream-processor
44else
45  docker compose restart redpanda
46fi
47fault_recovered="$(date +%s)"
48 
49wait "$inject_pid"
50cat "$output_file"
51echo "${case_name}_restart_seconds=$((fault_recovered - fault_started))"
52docker compose --profile evaluation run --rm evaluator report --wait 180

ops/resume_services.sh67 lines · SHA-256 cd8eb7c6f777

SHA-256: cd8eb7c6f777f6f115f92a824045ad2300ad20f34644d5fedea8a1a8b709df84

1#!/usr/bin/env bash
2set -euo pipefail
3 
4ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
5AWS_REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-west-2}"
6EKS_CLUSTER="${EKS_CLUSTER:-ai-governance-eks}"
7NODE_GROUP="${NODE_GROUP:-governance-spot-workers}"
8DB_INSTANCE="${DB_INSTANCE:-ai-governance-postgres}"
9NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-governance}"
10 
11cd "$ROOT_DIR"
12 
13docker compose up -d postgres >/dev/null
14aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$EKS_CLUSTER" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null
15 
16db_status="$(aws rds describe-db-instances \
17  --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
18  --region "$AWS_REGION" \
19  --query 'DBInstances[0].DBInstanceStatus' \
20  --output text)"
21if [[ "$db_status" == "stopped" ]]; then
22  aws rds start-db-instance \
23    --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
24    --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null
25fi
26 
27aws eks update-nodegroup-config \
28  --cluster-name "$EKS_CLUSTER" \
29  --nodegroup-name "$NODE_GROUP" \
30  --region "$AWS_REGION" \
31  --scaling-config minSize=3,maxSize=6,desiredSize=3 >/dev/null
32 
33aws eks wait nodegroup-active \
34  --cluster-name "$EKS_CLUSTER" \
35  --nodegroup-name "$NODE_GROUP" \
36  --region "$AWS_REGION"
37aws rds wait db-instance-available \
38  --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
39  --region "$AWS_REGION"
40kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node --all --timeout=600s >/dev/null
41 
42kubectl scale deployment governance-rule-engine -n "$NAMESPACE" --replicas=3 >/dev/null
43kubectl scale deployment governance-risk-scorer -n "$NAMESPACE" --replicas=1 >/dev/null
44kubectl scale deployment governance-postgres-sink -n "$NAMESPACE" --replicas=2 >/dev/null
45for adapter in \
46  keycloak-adapter \
47  kubernetes-audit-adapter \
48  airflow-openlineage-adapter \
49  model-registry-adapter \
50  llm-gateway-adapter; do
51  kubectl scale deployment "$adapter" -n "$NAMESPACE" --replicas=2 >/dev/null
52done
53 
54kubectl autoscale deployment governance-rule-engine -n "$NAMESPACE" \
55  --min=3 --max=6 --cpu-percent=70 >/dev/null
56for adapter in \
57  keycloak-adapter \
58  kubernetes-audit-adapter \
59  airflow-openlineage-adapter \
60  model-registry-adapter \
61  llm-gateway-adapter; do
62  kubectl autoscale deployment "$adapter" -n "$NAMESPACE" \
63    --min=2 --max=6 --cpu-percent=70 >/dev/null
64done
65 
66kubectl rollout status deployment --all -n "$NAMESPACE" --timeout=600s
67echo "AI governance services are running again."

services/postgres-sink/app.py141 lines · SHA-256 22628be07ba4

SHA-256: 22628be07ba431b2f2792ad0df92030c95b32c77b63a73c60aa0fecddab9ddc3

1from __future__ import annotations
2 
3import json
4import os
5import signal
6import time
7 
8from confluent_kafka import Consumer, KafkaError
9import psycopg
10from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
11 
12 
13RAW_TOPICS = [
14    "governance.keycloak.v1",
15    "governance.kubernetes.v1",
16    "governance.pipeline.v1",
17    "governance.model-registry.v1",
18    "governance.llm-gateway.v1",
19]
20FINDING_TOPIC = "governance.findings.scored.v1"
21running = True
22 
23 
24def kafka_config() -> dict:
25    config = {
26        "bootstrap.servers": os.getenv("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "localhost:19092"),
27        "security.protocol": os.getenv("KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL", "PLAINTEXT"),
28    }
29    if config["security.protocol"] != "PLAINTEXT":
30        from aws_msk_iam_sasl_signer import MSKAuthTokenProvider
31 
32        region = os.environ["AWS_REGION"]
33 
34        def oauth_cb(_):
35            token, expiry_ms = MSKAuthTokenProvider.generate_auth_token(region)
36            return token, expiry_ms / 1000
37 
38        config.update({"sasl.mechanism": "OAUTHBEARER", "oauth_cb": oauth_cb})
39    return config
40 
41 
42def connect_database():
43    dsn = os.getenv("POSTGRES_DSN", "postgresql://governance:governance@localhost:5432/governance")
44    while running:
45        try:
46            return psycopg.connect(dsn, autocommit=False)
47        except psycopg.OperationalError:
48            time.sleep(2)
49    raise RuntimeError("Stopping before database became available")
50 
51 
52def write_raw(connection, event: dict) -> None:
53    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
54        cursor.execute(
55            """
56            INSERT INTO raw_events
57              (event_id, schema_version, producer, event_type, event_time, ingested_at,
58               environment, correlation_id, payload)
59            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
60            ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING
61            """,
62            (
63                event["event_id"], event["schema_version"], event["producer"], event["event_type"],
64                event["event_time"], event["ingested_at"], event["environment"],
65                event["correlation_id"], Jsonb(event),
66            ),
67        )
68 
69 
70def write_finding(connection, finding: dict) -> None:
71    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
72        cursor.execute(
73            """
74            INSERT INTO compliance_findings
75              (finding_id, rule_id, title, producer, source_event_id, source_event_time,
76               detected_at, window_start, window_end, severity, severity_label, frequency,
77               frequency_band, baseline_risk, isolation_forest_risk, risk_delta,
78               recommended_risk, model_status, frameworks, evidence)
79            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
80            ON CONFLICT (finding_id) DO UPDATE SET
81              isolation_forest_risk = EXCLUDED.isolation_forest_risk,
82              risk_delta = EXCLUDED.risk_delta,
83              recommended_risk = EXCLUDED.recommended_risk,
84              model_status = EXCLUDED.model_status,
85              persisted_at = now()
86            """,
87            (
88                finding["finding_id"], finding["rule_id"], finding["title"], finding["producer"],
89                finding["source_event_id"], finding["source_event_time"], finding["detected_at"],
90                finding.get("window_start"), finding.get("window_end"), finding["severity"],
91                finding["severity_label"], finding["frequency"], finding["frequency_band"],
92                finding["baseline_risk"], finding.get("isolation_forest_risk"), finding.get("risk_delta"),
93                finding.get("recommended_risk", finding["baseline_risk"]), finding.get("model_status"),
94                Jsonb(finding["frameworks"]), Jsonb(finding["evidence"]),
95            ),
96        )
97 
98 
99def stop(*_):
100    global running
101    running = False
102 
103 
104def main() -> None:
105    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
106    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
107    consumer = Consumer({
108        **kafka_config(),
109        "group.id": os.getenv("KAFKA_GROUP_ID", "governance-postgres-sink-v1"),
110        "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
111        "enable.auto.commit": False,
112    })
113    consumer.subscribe(RAW_TOPICS + [FINDING_TOPIC])
114    connection = connect_database()
115    try:
116        while running:
117            message = consumer.poll(1.0)
118            if message is None:
119                continue
120            if message.error():
121                if message.error().code() not in (KafkaError._PARTITION_EOF, KafkaError.UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PART):
122                    raise RuntimeError(message.error())
123                continue
124            payload = json.loads(message.value())
125            try:
126                if message.topic() == FINDING_TOPIC:
127                    write_finding(connection, payload)
128                else:
129                    write_raw(connection, payload)
130                connection.commit()
131                consumer.commit(message=message, asynchronous=False)
132            except (psycopg.OperationalError, psycopg.InterfaceError):
133                connection.close()
134                connection = connect_database()
135    finally:
136        connection.close()
137        consumer.close()
138 
139 
140if __name__ == "__main__":
141    main()
